newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT-Dlr/mark seen targeting 1.59 next week.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Dlr/mark seen targeting 1.59 next week.

text.p: The dollar hurdled a major barrier at 1.5825/35 marks to hit a 29-month high of 1.5873 marks in late U.S. trade, with further gains expected next week, technical analysts said on Friday.

The uptrend may pause early next week, but will eventually resume with the U.S. unit challenging formidable channel-line resistance at 1.5870/75 marks and, past that, a tough psychological barrier around the 1.59 figure, chartists said.

"We may get a weak start next week, but I believe we will move on and penetrate 1.5870/75 marks and then perhaps to even bigger and better things," said Randolph Donney, director of capital markets research at Pegasus Econometric Group.
Darren Spain, a technical analyst at Credit Suisse, said he foresees dollar/mark short-term momentum intact until resistance at 1.5895 to 1.5905 marks, the August 14, 1994 high.
"The short-term uptrend is intact and could reach 1.59 to even 1.5940 (marks) -- or until we get a breakdown in momentum," Spain said.

Donney said the last major swing high on the monthly charts is 1.7673 marks. He called the chance to revisit that level "pie in the sky" but said the dollar could rise a third to a half of the distance to that goal.
Dollar/mark support was quoted at 1.58 and 1.5730, Europe's low on Friday.
Against the yen, the dollar waffled around the 116 figure, keeping well within the week's narrow trading range.
Most analysts viewed dollar/yen's lackluster performance since hitting a 45-month peak of 117 on Monday as a gearing up for another push to long-term targets between 118 to 120 yen.
"We are viewing this week as a consolidative week and effectively we stayed within Monday's ranges. Our view is the consolidation is constructive as long as we hold above 114.90 (yen)," Spain said.
Donney projected continued dollar/yen range trading between 114.85 and 117, until the dollar eventually breaks-out on the upside.
